title: Transhumanist Party Sample Ballot
description: A sample ballot with a question of each kind: a ranked choice, a choice of one, a committee where members choose several, and three platform planks to vote yes, no or abstain on. Every candidate is invented and no plank is party policy: change them before using this for a real election.

contests.title: Party Chair
contests.description: Rank the candidates in order of preference. If your first choice is eliminated, your vote goes to your next.

candidates.name: Aurelia Dawnmere
candidates.statement: Organizer of a longevity research reading group. Wants every national meeting open to members online.

candidates.name: Bastian Helixford
candidates.statement: Science teacher. Wants a party chapter in every state before the next convention.

candidates.name: Isolde Northvane
candidates.statement: Bioethicist. Will publish what the party spends every quarter.

contests.title: Host city for the next national convention
contests.description: Choose one. The city with the most votes hosts the convention.

contests.title: Science and Technology Committee (3 seats)
contests.description: Choose up to three. The three with the most votes join the committee.

candidates.name: Calla Brightwater
candidates.statement: Gerontologist. Would review the platform’s health planks.

candidates.name: Dorian Ironvale
candidates.statement: Software engineer working on open-source AI tools.

candidates.name: Galen Moonfield
candidates.statement: Materials scientist with an eye on settling space.

candidates.name: Marisol Oakhaven
candidates.statement: Science journalist. Would write the committee’s reports for members.

contests.title: Plank: Morphological freedom
contests.description: Should the platform include this plank? It passes with more than half of the yes and no votes.

proposal.body:
Every person has the right to keep, change and enhance their own body and mind, by medical, technological or other means, as long as they do not harm others. The law should not forbid an informed adult’s choice of an enhancement that is safe for others.

Sample text for trying out the ballot. It is not party policy.

contests.title: Plank: Public funding for rejuvenation research
contests.description: Should the platform include this plank? It passes with two thirds of the yes and no votes.

proposal.body:
Aging causes more death and disease than anything else. Public research budgets should treat the biology of aging as a target for medicine, and fund therapies that slow, stop or reverse it, with the results published openly.

Sample text for trying out the ballot. It is not party policy.

contests.title: Plank: Open research into AI safety
contests.description: Should the platform include this plank? It passes with more than half of the yes and no votes, if at least a quarter of the voter roll votes on it.

proposal.body:
Research into making advanced artificial intelligence safe should be publicly funded and openly published, so that anyone can check it and build on it.

Sample text for trying out the ballot. It is not party policy.
